title: Squeaky's Lost Day
markdown:
The late afternoon sun painted soft golden patterns on Rowan’s warm wooden floor. Her little cottage in the gentle hills smelled of sweet pine and damp earth after quiet rain. Rowan was a kind witch. Her magic helped tiny seeds open and warmed cold toes, not loud booming spells. Today she lined dewdrop charms on the windowsill. She believed the best magic was simply being kind.

Then a tiny worried squeak. A very small mouse shivered there, fur soft and grey like a little cloud, whiskers twitching. Lost, far from a cozy home. Rowan knew she had to help.

She opened the window. Sweet evening air. “Hello, little one. Are you lost, little friend?” Another squeak, a clear Yes. She scooped the mouse into warm hands, light as a leaf. “I’ll call you Squeaky.” Nose twitch. “We must find your home before the moon wakes up.” Kindness takes its time.

Squeaky, though sweet, was a little stubborn. He scampered ahead, then stopped, sniffing. Rowan followed a faint scent like dandelion fluff. Winding paths through whispering pines, needles murmuring secrets—helping, or playful gossip?

From behind a mossy rock: Wizard Fitzwilliam, long white beard nearly sweeping the ground. “Hello, Rowan! Out for a walk with a new friend?” She explained. He nodded, rummaged. Maps tumbled: stars, underground rivers, places only in dreams. A map drawn on a leaf. “Follow this wiggly line, past the giggling brook and under the sleeping owl tree. We’ll be there fast!” He gave her a map that looked like a happy dragon. The directions led in funny circles. Her lantern glowed, shadows like happy fireflies. Kindness takes its time.

Moon peeking, purple and pink. Pines taller. Path harder to see. Squeaky snuggled in her pocket, a tiny ball of warmth. “We’ve wandered a little far.” The lantern a small pool in the dimness.

Tangled leafy bushes. She sat on moss, set Squeaky on fallen leaves. Bright black eyes, trusting. She hadn’t brought him home tonight as promised. Light seemed to dim.

A gentle sigh. “It seems we won’t find your cozy home tonight, little Squeaky.” A soft woven blanket around them both, like a hug. “You’ll be safe and warm with me. We’ll try our very best in the morning, when the sun is high and the path is clear.” A smooth warm pebble from her pocket. He nibbled, curled against her hand. Kindness takes its time.

Next morning, sun on the hills, a happy squeak. Squeaky pointed his tiny nose toward mossy rocks. Nestled between them: a tiny perfect mouse-sized door with a green leaf for a roof. “Squeaky! Your home! It was so close all along!”

Fitzwilliam ambled by, sorting scrolls, pleased. “I’ve finally sorted my maps! Your friend’s home was right here. My map of Hidden Homes of the Forest was tucked neatly under Where the Cloud Sheep Graze.” A dry chuckle. Muddled maps, a surprising journey, not entirely the wrong one.

She placed Squeaky at his little door. A happy grateful goodbye, and he scampered in. Rowan waved. Fitzwilliam was already talking to a busy beetle about the Whispering Waterfall. The hills felt peaceful and bright. Kindness takes its time, and sometimes the door is just past the moss.
